```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local rig of the pre-deploy verification (plan Phase 8). Lives outside both repos; never committed.
# The UI redesign's release gate (its plan Phase 11) runs it for the combined release: the SPA is the
# ui-frontend worktree, the backend image is built in the ui-release worktree, and every SPA build
# sets VITE_CARD_ART_BASE_URL (UI-redesign P-4).
#
#   up                         pd-mongo (mongo:8.0, single-node replica set rs0) on 127.0.0.1:27018,
#                              pd-redis (redis:7-alpine) on 127.0.0.1:6380, pd-mailpit (SMTP on
#                              pd-mailpit:587 inside the rig network, published on 127.0.0.1:1025;
#                              API and UI on 127.0.0.1:8025), all on the docker network pd-rig
#   build-image <sha>          a clean detached worktree of the backend at <sha> (ui-release), and
#                              the image stiglja-api:rig built there
#   image-checks               R-2 AC3 (Java 21, not root, no .env* in the jar) and R-1 AC3
#                              (availableProcessors() = 4, MaxHeapSize about 70 % of 1 GiB)
#   dummy-env-check            R-2 AC4: a .env in the build context reaches no layer
#   backend-start [jwt-min]    (re)creates pd-backend on 127.0.0.1:8080 with exactly R-4's env
#   backend-stop               docker stop pd-backend (SIGTERM, graceful)
#   backend-restart-after <s>  stop, <s> seconds down, start again, wait until it is up
#   r4-checks                  R-4 AC1, AC2 and AC4
#   sigterm-check              R-3 AC3
#   idle-check                 R-1 AC3: still up after 10 idle minutes at 1 GiB
#   spa-build                  the SPA worktree's production build for the rig: the API at
#                              http://localhost:8080, the card art from CARD_ART
#   spa-check                  R-28 AC3: the deep link, the title, the bundle's API origin, CORS;
#                              P-4: the bundle's card-art origin
#   spa-preview                fallback only: vite preview of the SPA worktree outside the sandbox
#   logs <label> [dir]         saves pd-backend's log as backend-<label>.log (in dir, default here)
#   status                     the rig containers
#   down                       removes the rig containers, the network and the ui-release worktree
#
# Never port 27017: an unrelated container owns it. Every wait is bounded. No secret is ever
# printed: the JWT secret lives in rig-jwt.secret (mode 600) and reaches docker only through the
# docker client's environment.
set -u

LOGS=/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/logs/pre-deploy
BE_REPO=/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja
FE_WT=/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/ui-frontend
RELEASE_WT=/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/ui-release
NET=pd-rig
IMAGE=stiglja-api:rig
BUILDER=desktop-linux
SECRET_FILE=$LOGS/rig-jwt.secret
SPA_ORIGIN=http://localhost:4173
# The card art's origin for every SPA build on the rig (UI-redesign P-4): the r2.dev bucket until the
# custom domain exists (pre-deploy Phase 9 as amended); a production build without it stops.
CARD_ART=https://pub-35c6a55a85654bcaa462dcc5f31c7c71.r2.dev/v1
API=http://127.0.0.1:8080
JAVA_OPTS='-XX:ActiveProcessorCount=4 -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70'
# R-4 AC1's env plus fly.toml's JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, in LC_ALL=C sort order
EXPECTED_ENV='APP_BASE_URL CORS_ALLOWEDORIGINS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS JWT_SECRET MAIL_FROM MAIL_HOST REDIS_LINK REDIS_PASS REDIS_PORT REDIS_USER SIGNUP_INVITE_CODE SPRING_DATA_MONGODB_URI'
FAILS=0

die()  { echo "rig: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
pass() { echo "PASS $*"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL $*"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); }
result() { echo "RESULT $1: $FAILS failures"; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]; }
# http <url> [max seconds]: the status code, 000 when nothing answered
http() { curl --noproxy '*' -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time "${2:-30}" "$1"; }
now() { python3 -c 'import time; print(time.time())'; }
seconds_between() { python3 -c 'import sys; print("%.1f" % (float(sys.argv[2]) - float(sys.argv[1])))' "$1" "$2"; }
# within <value> <low> <high>: low <= value <= high
within() { python3 -c 'import sys; v, lo, hi = map(float, sys.argv[1:]); sys.exit(0 if lo <= v <= hi else 1)' "$1" "$2" "$3"; }

wait_for() {  # wait_for <seconds> <what> <command...>: retries the command once a second
  local limit=$1 what=$2 i=0
  shift 2
  while [ "$i" -lt "$limit" ]; do
    "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    sleep 1
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  die "timed out after ${limit} s waiting for: $what"
}

mongo_ping()    { docker exec pd-mongo mongosh --quiet --eval 'db.runCommand({ping:1}).ok' | /usr/bin/grep -qx 1; }
mongo_primary() { docker exec pd-mongo mongosh --quiet --eval 'db.hello().isWritablePrimary' | /usr/bin/grep -qx true; }
redis_ping()    { docker exec pd-redis redis-cli ping | /usr/bin/grep -qx PONG; }
mailpit_up()    { [ "$(http http://127.0.0.1:8025/api/v1/info 5)" = 200 ]; }
live_up()       { [ "$(http "$API/actuator/health/liveness" 5)" = 200 ]; }
ready_up()      { [ "$(http "$API/actuator/health/readiness" 5)" = 200 ]; }
stream_open()   { /usr/bin/grep -qx o "$1"; }
started_count() { docker logs pd-backend 2>&1 | /usr/bin/grep -c 'Started BelatroApplication'; }
running()       { [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' pd-backend 2>/dev/null)" = true ]; }

wait_started() {  # wait_started <Started lines before>: one more Started line, then liveness 200
  local before=$1 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt 180 ]; do
    if [ "$(started_count)" -gt "$before" ]; then
      wait_for 30 "GET /actuator/health/liveness = 200" live_up
      echo "pd-backend up: $(docker logs pd-backend 2>&1 | /usr/bin/grep -o 'Started BelatroApplication in [0-9.]* seconds' | tail -1)"
      return 0
    fi
    running || break
    sleep 1
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  docker logs --tail 80 pd-backend >&2
  die "pd-backend did not start within 180 s (its last 80 log lines are above)"
}

cmd_up() {
  docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "Docker is not running: the owner starts Docker Desktop"
  docker rm -f pd-backend pd-mongo pd-redis pd-mailpit >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 1
  local port
  for port in 27018 6380 1025 8025 8080; do
    if lsof -nP -iTCP:"$port" -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      lsof -nP -iTCP:"$port" -sTCP:LISTEN >&2
      die "port $port is taken by the process above: find out whose it is and stop it first (never another agent's)"
    fi
  done
  docker network inspect "$NET" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create "$NET" >/dev/null \
    || die "cannot create the network $NET"
  docker run -d --name pd-mongo --network "$NET" -p 127.0.0.1:27018:27017 mongo:8.0 --replSet rs0 --bind_ip_all \
    >/dev/null || die "pd-mongo did not start"
  docker run -d --name pd-redis --network "$NET" -p 127.0.0.1:6380:6379 redis:7-alpine \
    >/dev/null || die "pd-redis did not start"
  # SMTP on 587: the backend's default port when MAIL_PORT is unset, as with Brevo in production,
  # so the backend runs with R-4's env and no MAIL_PORT.
  docker run -d --name pd-mailpit --network "$NET" -p 127.0.0.1:1025:587 -p 127.0.0.1:8025:8025 \
    axllent/mailpit:v1.31 --smtp 0.0.0.0:587 >/dev/null || die "pd-mailpit did not start"
  wait_for 60 "Mongo answers ping" mongo_ping
  # One member, registered as localhost:27017 inside its own container. The backend connects with
  # directConnection=true, so it never follows that member address.
  docker exec pd-mongo mongosh --quiet --eval \
    'try { rs.status().ok } catch (e) { rs.initiate({_id: "rs0", members: [{_id: 0, host: "localhost:27017"}]}).ok }' \
    >/dev/null || die "rs.initiate failed"
  wait_for 60 "Mongo is a writable primary" mongo_primary
  wait_for 30 "Redis answers PING" redis_ping
  wait_for 30 "the Mailpit API answers" mailpit_up
  echo "rig up: pd-mongo 127.0.0.1:27018 (rs0 primary), pd-redis 127.0.0.1:6380, pd-mailpit SMTP pd-mailpit:587 / API 127.0.0.1:8025, network $NET"
}

cmd_build_image() {
  local sha=${1:-}
  [ -n "$sha" ] || die "usage: rig.sh build-image <backend sha>"
  git -C "$BE_REPO" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || die "$sha is not a commit of $BE_REPO"
  if [ -e "$RELEASE_WT" ]; then
    git -C "$BE_REPO" worktree remove --force "$RELEASE_WT" || die "cannot remove the old $RELEASE_WT"
  fi
  git -C "$BE_REPO" worktree add --detach "$RELEASE_WT" "$sha" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || die "git worktree add $RELEASE_WT $sha failed"
  [ -z "$(git -C "$RELEASE_WT" status --porcelain --ignored)" ] || die "$RELEASE_WT is not clean"
  if ls -A "$RELEASE_WT" | /usr/bin/grep -q '^\.env'; then die "an .env file in $RELEASE_WT: STOP"; fi
  echo "release worktree $RELEASE_WT at $(git -C "$RELEASE_WT" rev-parse HEAD): clean, no .env*"
  if ! docker buildx build --builder "$BUILDER" --load -t "$IMAGE" "$RELEASE_WT" > "$LOGS/docker-build.log" 2>&1; then
    tail -40 "$LOGS/docker-build.log" >&2
    die "docker build failed (full log: $LOGS/docker-build.log)"
  fi
  git -C "$RELEASE_WT" rev-parse HEAD > "$LOGS/release-image-sha.txt"
  echo "built $IMAGE from $(cat "$LOGS/release-image-sha.txt") ($(docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "$IMAGE"))"
}

cmd_image_checks() {
  docker image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "no $IMAGE: run build-image first"
  local version uid jar cid listing procs heap ratio
  # R-2 AC3: Java 21, not root, no .env* inside the jar
  version=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint java "$IMAGE" -version 2>&1 | head -1)
  case "$version" in
    *'version "21.'*) pass "R-2 AC3 java -version: $version" ;;
    *) fail "R-2 AC3 java -version: $version" ;;
  esac
  uid=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint id "$IMAGE" -u)
  if [ -n "$uid" ] && [ "$uid" != 0 ]; then pass "R-2 AC3 id -u = $uid"; else fail "R-2 AC3 id -u = '$uid'"; fi
  jar=$LOGS/release-app.jar
  rm -f "$jar"
  cid=$(docker create "$IMAGE") || die "docker create $IMAGE failed"
  docker cp "$cid:/app/app.jar" "$jar" >/dev/null 2>&1
  docker rm "$cid" >/dev/null
  [ -s "$jar" ] || die "could not copy /app/app.jar out of $IMAGE"
  # the runtime image has no unzip: list the copied jar with python's zipfile
  listing=$(python3 - "$jar" <<'PY'
import sys, zipfile
names = zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).namelist()
env = [n for n in names if n.rstrip('/').rsplit('/', 1)[-1].startswith('.env')]
print(len(names), len(env), ' '.join(env))
PY
)
  set -- $listing
  if [ "${2:-x}" = 0 ]; then pass "R-2 AC3 jar: $1 entries, none named .env*"; else fail "R-2 AC3 jar entries named .env*: $listing"; fi
  # R-1 AC3: the JRE has no jshell, so a compiled probe class runs in the image itself
  mkdir -p "$LOGS/probe"
  cat > "$LOGS/probe/Probe.java" <<'JAVA'
public class Probe {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("availableProcessors=" + Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors());
    }
}
JAVA
  docker run --rm -v "$LOGS/probe:/probe" -w /probe eclipse-temurin:21-jdk javac -d /probe /probe/Probe.java \
    >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "javac of the probe failed"
  procs=$(docker run --rm -m 1g -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="$JAVA_OPTS" -v "$LOGS/probe:/probe:ro" --entrypoint java \
    "$IMAGE" -cp /probe Probe 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^availableProcessors=//p')
  if [ "$procs" = 4 ]; then pass "R-1 AC3 availableProcessors() = 4 in a -m 1g container with JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS"
  else fail "R-1 AC3 availableProcessors() = '$procs'"; fi
  heap=$(docker run --rm -m 1g -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="$JAVA_OPTS" --entrypoint java "$IMAGE" \
    -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version 2>/dev/null | awk '$2 == "MaxHeapSize" {print $4}')
  ratio=$(python3 -c 'import sys; print("%.3f" % (int(sys.argv[1] or 0) / 1073741824))' "${heap:-0}")
  if within "$ratio" 0.68 0.72; then pass "R-1 AC3 MaxHeapSize = $heap bytes = $ratio of 1 GiB"
  else fail "R-1 AC3 MaxHeapSize = '$heap' bytes = $ratio of 1 GiB"; fi
  result image-checks
}

# new_env_files <image> <its base image>: the .env* paths in <image> that the base does not have
new_env_files() {
  LC_ALL=C comm -13 \
    <(docker run --rm --user 0 --entrypoint sh "$2" -c "find / -xdev -name '.env*' 2>/dev/null" | LC_ALL=C sort) \
    <(docker run --rm --user 0 --entrypoint sh "$1" -c "find / -xdev -name '.env*' 2>/dev/null" | LC_ALL=C sort)
}

cmd_dummy_env_check() {
  [ -d "$RELEASE_WT" ] || die "no $RELEASE_WT: run build-image first"
  local ok=1 found
  printf 'RIG_DUMMY_MUST_NOT_SHIP=1\n' > "$RELEASE_WT/.env"
  printf 'RIG_DUMMY_MUST_NOT_SHIP=1\n' > "$RELEASE_WT/.env.docker"
  docker buildx build --builder "$BUILDER" --load --target build -t stiglja-api:rig-builder "$RELEASE_WT" \
    > "$LOGS/docker-build-dummy-builder.log" 2>&1 || ok=0
  docker buildx build --builder "$BUILDER" --load -t stiglja-api:rig-dummy "$RELEASE_WT" \
    > "$LOGS/docker-build-dummy.log" 2>&1 || ok=0
  rm -f "$RELEASE_WT/.env" "$RELEASE_WT/.env.docker"
  [ "$ok" = 1 ] || die "a build with the dummy .env failed (logs: $LOGS/docker-build-dummy*.log)"
  found=$(new_env_files stiglja-api:rig-builder eclipse-temurin:21-jdk)
  if [ -z "$found" ]; then pass "R-2 AC4 builder stage: no .env* file beyond its base image's"; else fail "R-2 AC4 builder stage has: $found"; fi
  found=$(new_env_files stiglja-api:rig-dummy eclipse-temurin:21-jre)
  if [ -z "$found" ]; then pass "R-2 AC4 final image: no .env* file beyond its base image's"; else fail "R-2 AC4 final image has: $found"; fi
  # Only the history lines this Dockerfile adds, as for the file checks above: the base image's own
  # history carries Ubuntu's `umoci config … --config.env PATH=…`, which is not ours. (8.4 deviation)
  local hist base
  hist=$(docker history --no-trunc --format '{{.CreatedBy}}' stiglja-api:rig-dummy)
  base=$(docker history --no-trunc --format '{{.CreatedBy}}' eclipse-temurin:21-jre)
  if [ -z "$hist" ] || [ -z "$base" ]; then
    fail "R-2 AC4 docker history unreadable (stiglja-api:rig-dummy or eclipse-temurin:21-jre)"
  else
    found=$(printf '%s\n' "$hist" | /usr/bin/grep -vxF -f <(printf '%s\n' "$base") | /usr/bin/grep '\.env')
    if [ -n "$found" ]; then
      fail "R-2 AC4 docker history mentions .env: $found"
    else
      pass "R-2 AC4 docker history mentions no .env beyond its base image's"
    fi
  fi
  if [ -z "$(git -C "$RELEASE_WT" status --porcelain --ignored)" ]; then pass "R-2 AC4 the release worktree is clean again"
  else fail "R-2 AC4 the release worktree is not clean after the check"; fi
  docker image rm stiglja-api:rig-builder stiglja-api:rig-dummy >/dev/null 2>&1
  result dummy-env-check
}

cmd_backend_start() {
  local minutes=${1:-}
  case "$minutes" in ''|[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9][0-9]) ;; *) die "usage: rig.sh backend-start [jwt-minutes]" ;; esac
  docker image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "no $IMAGE: run build-image first"
  docker container inspect pd-mongo pd-redis pd-mailpit >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "the rig is not up: run 'rig.sh up'"
  if [ ! -s "$SECRET_FILE" ]; then
    (umask 077 && openssl rand -base64 48 > "$SECRET_FILE") || die "cannot write $SECRET_FILE"
  fi
  docker rm -f pd-backend >/dev/null 2>&1
  JWT_SECRET=$(cat "$SECRET_FILE")
  export JWT_SECRET
  # JWT_EXPIRATION only for the R-10 run: docker 28 records a bare "-e NAME" in the container's
  # env even when NAME is unset, so the flag itself is left out otherwise. (8.5 deviation)
  set --
  if [ -n "$minutes" ]; then set -- -e "JWT_EXPIRATION=$minutes"; fi
  # Exactly spec R-4 AC1's env, plus fly.toml's JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS (and JWT_EXPIRATION for R-10
  # only). The three --spring.mail... arguments are not env on purpose: only Mailpit needs them
  # (no STARTTLS, no AUTH; production's Brevo has both), and relaxed binding cannot express the
  # dotted mail.smtp.* keys as environment variables.
  docker run -d --name pd-backend --network "$NET" -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -m 1g --cpus 1 --stop-timeout 15 \
    -e JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="$JAVA_OPTS" \
    -e 'SPRING_DATA_MONGODB_URI=mongodb://pd-mongo:27017/belatro?directConnection=true&serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000' \
    -e REDIS_LINK=pd-redis -e REDIS_PORT=6379 -e REDIS_USER= -e REDIS_PASS= \
    -e JWT_SECRET "$@" \
    -e MAIL_HOST=pd-mailpit -e 'MAIL_FROM=Stiglja <no-reply@stiglja.com>' \
    -e APP_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4173 -e CORS_ALLOWEDORIGINS=http://localhost:4173 \
    -e SIGNUP_INVITE_CODE=rig-invite \
    "$IMAGE" \
    --spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.starttls.enable=false \
    --spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.starttls.required=false \
    --spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.auth=false >/dev/null || die "docker run pd-backend failed"
  unset JWT_SECRET
  wait_started 0
  if [ -n "$minutes" ]; then echo "pd-backend: JWT_EXPIRATION=$minutes minutes"; fi
}

cmd_backend_restart_after() {
  local secs=${1:-} before
  case "$secs" in ''|*[!0-9]*) die "usage: rig.sh backend-restart-after <seconds>" ;; esac
  before=$(started_count)
  docker stop pd-backend >/dev/null || die "docker stop pd-backend failed"
  echo "pd-backend stopped (SIGTERM, graceful); down for $secs s"
  sleep "$secs"
  docker start pd-backend >/dev/null || die "docker start pd-backend failed"
  wait_started "$before"
}

login_probe() {  # POST /api/auth/login for an unknown user (it reads users): "<status> <seconds>"
  curl --noproxy '*' -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}' --max-time 60 \
    -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"rig_nobody","password":"wrong-password-1"}' \
    "$API/api/auth/login"
}

cmd_r4_checks() {
  local added status t secs
  cmd_backend_start
  # AC1: the container's own env names (values never printed) are exactly R-4's list
  added=$(LC_ALL=C comm -13 \
    <(docker image inspect -f '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' "$IMAGE" | sed -e 's/=.*//' -e '/^$/d' | LC_ALL=C sort) \
    <(docker container inspect -f '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' pd-backend | sed -e 's/=.*//' -e '/^$/d' | LC_ALL=C sort) \
    | tr '\n' ' ')
  if [ "$added" = "$EXPECTED_ENV " ]; then pass "R-4 AC1 started with exactly these env names: $added"
  else fail "R-4 AC1 env names '$added', expected '$EXPECTED_ENV '"; fi
  # The ApplicationReadyEvent listeners (index setup, timer re-arm, queue warm-up) run after the
  # "Started" line; until they finish, readiness and so the full health are OUT_OF_SERVICE (503).
  # (8.5 deviation: the first run raced them)
  wait_for 30 "GET /actuator/health/readiness = 200" ready_up
  status=$(http "$API/actuator/health" 30)
  if [ "$status" = 200 ]; then pass "R-4 AC1 GET /actuator/health = 200 (Mongo, Redis and Mailpit up)"
  else fail "R-4 AC1 GET /actuator/health = $status"; fi
  # AC2: Redis stopped -> liveness stays 200, the full health is 503
  docker stop pd-redis >/dev/null || die "docker stop pd-redis failed"
  status=$(http "$API/actuator/health/liveness" 30)
  if [ "$status" = 200 ]; then pass "R-4 AC2 GET /actuator/health/liveness = 200 with Redis stopped"
  else fail "R-4 AC2 GET /actuator/health/liveness = $status with Redis stopped"; fi
  t=$(curl --noproxy '*' -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}' --max-time 90 "$API/actuator/health")
  case "$t" in
    '503 '*) pass "R-4 AC2 GET /actuator/health = 503 with Redis stopped (${t#* } s)" ;;
    *) fail "R-4 AC2 GET /actuator/health = ${t% *} with Redis stopped (${t#* } s)" ;;
  esac
  docker start pd-redis >/dev/null || die "docker start pd-redis failed"
  wait_for 30 "Redis answers PING again" redis_ping
  # AC4: Mongo paused -> a request that reads Mongo fails after ~5 s of server selection, not 30 s.
  # The driver first has to notice the silent server (its monitor times out within ~20 s), so the
  # timed request is made 30 s after the pause.
  t=$(login_probe)
  status=${t% *}; secs=${t#* }
  if [ "$status" != 200 ] && [ "$status" != 000 ] && within "$secs" 0 3; then
    pass "R-4 AC4 baseline with Mongo up: POST /api/auth/login = $status in $secs s"
  else fail "R-4 AC4 baseline with Mongo up: POST /api/auth/login = $status in $secs s"; fi
  docker pause pd-mongo >/dev/null || die "docker pause pd-mongo failed"
  sleep 30
  t=$(login_probe)
  docker unpause pd-mongo >/dev/null || die "docker unpause pd-mongo failed"
  status=${t% *}; secs=${t#* }
  if [ "$status" != 200 ] && [ "$status" != 000 ] && within "$secs" 4 9; then
    pass "R-4 AC4 with Mongo paused: POST /api/auth/login = $status after $secs s"
  else fail "R-4 AC4 with Mongo paused: POST /api/auth/login = $status after $secs s (expected an error after 4-9 s)"; fi
  wait_for 60 "Mongo answers ping again" mongo_ping
  docker logs pd-backend > "$LOGS/backend-r4.log" 2>&1
  result r4-checks
}

cmd_sigterm_check() {
  local out=$LOGS/sigterm-xhr-stream.txt t0 t1 elapsed code i=0
  cmd_backend_start
  : > "$out"
  # one SockJS xhr_streaming client: a POST the server keeps open, as a browser without WebSocket does
  curl --noproxy '*' -sN -X POST -H "Origin: $SPA_ORIGIN" "$API/ws/000/rigsigterm$$/xhr_streaming" > "$out" 2>&1 &
  CURL_PID=$!
  trap 'kill "${CURL_PID:-}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
  wait_for 15 "the xhr_streaming client gets the SockJS open frame" stream_open "$out"
  pass "R-3 AC3 one SockJS xhr_streaming client is connected (open frame received)"
  t0=$(now)
  docker kill -s TERM pd-backend >/dev/null || die "docker kill -s TERM pd-backend failed"
  while [ "$i" -lt 300 ] && running; do
    sleep 0.1
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  t1=$(now)
  elapsed=$(seconds_between "$t0" "$t1")
  code=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.ExitCode}}' pd-backend)
  if ! running && within "$elapsed" 0 15; then pass "R-3 AC3 the container stopped $elapsed s after SIGTERM (exit code $code)"
  else fail "R-3 AC3 the container was still running $elapsed s after SIGTERM"; fi
  docker logs pd-backend 2>&1 | /usr/bin/grep -i -E 'graceful shutdown|outbox' > "$LOGS/sigterm-shutdown-lines.txt"
  echo "shutdown log lines: $LOGS/sigterm-shutdown-lines.txt"
  result sigterm-check
}

cmd_idle_check() {
  local started state stats status
  cmd_backend_start
  started=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' pd-backend)
  echo "idling 600 s from $(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
  sleep 600
  state=$(docker inspect -f 'running={{.State.Running}} oomkilled={{.State.OOMKilled}} restarts={{.RestartCount}} startedAt={{.State.StartedAt}}' pd-backend)
  stats=$(docker stats --no-stream --format 'mem={{.MemUsage}} ({{.MemPerc}}) cpu={{.CPUPerc}}' pd-backend)
  status=$(http "$API/actuator/health/liveness" 10)
  case "$state" in
    "running=true oomkilled=false restarts=0 startedAt=$started") pass "R-1 AC3 up after 10 idle minutes at 1 GiB: $state; $stats" ;;
    *) fail "R-1 AC3 after 10 idle minutes: $state (started at $started); $stats" ;;
  esac
  if [ "$status" = 200 ]; then pass "R-1 AC3 GET /actuator/health/liveness = 200 after 10 minutes"
  else fail "R-1 AC3 GET /actuator/health/liveness = $status after 10 minutes"; fi
  docker logs pd-backend > "$LOGS/backend-idle.log" 2>&1
  result idle-check
}

cmd_spa_check() {
  running || die "pd-backend is not running: run 'rig.sh backend-start' first"
  local status page pre
  status=$(http "$SPA_ORIGIN/confirm-email?token=x" 10)
  if [ "$status" = 200 ]; then pass "R-28 AC3 GET $SPA_ORIGIN/confirm-email?token=x = 200"
  else fail "R-28 AC3 GET $SPA_ORIGIN/confirm-email?token=x = $status"; fi
  page=$(curl --noproxy '*' -s --max-time 10 "$SPA_ORIGIN/confirm-email?token=x")
  case "$page" in
    *'<div id="root"></div>'*) pass "R-28 AC3 the deep link serves the SPA shell" ;;
    *) fail "R-28 AC3 the deep link does not serve the SPA shell" ;;
  esac
  case "$page" in
    *'<title>Stiglja</title>'*) pass "R-39 the shell's title is Stiglja" ;;
    *) fail "R-39 the shell has no <title>Stiglja</title>" ;;
  esac
  if /usr/bin/grep -rlq 'http://localhost:8080' "$FE_WT/dist/assets"; then pass "R-28 the served bundle (dist/assets) calls http://localhost:8080"
  else fail "R-28 no file in $FE_WT/dist/assets names http://localhost:8080"; fi
  if /usr/bin/grep -rlqF "$CARD_ART" "$FE_WT/dist/assets"; then pass "P-4 the served bundle (dist/assets) loads its card art from $CARD_ART"
  else fail "P-4 no file in $FE_WT/dist/assets names $CARD_ART"; fi
  pre=$(curl --noproxy '*' -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 -X OPTIONS "$API/api/auth/login" \
    -H "Origin: $SPA_ORIGIN" -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST')
  if [ "$pre" = 200 ]; then pass "R-28 CORS preflight from $SPA_ORIGIN = 200"; else fail "R-28 CORS preflight from $SPA_ORIGIN = $pre"; fi
  pre=$(curl --noproxy '*' -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 -X OPTIONS "$API/api/auth/login" \
    -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST')
  if [ "$pre" = 403 ]; then pass "R-28 CORS preflight from https://evil.example = 403"; else fail "R-28 CORS preflight from https://evil.example = $pre"; fi
  result spa-check
}

cmd_spa_build() {
  cd "$FE_WT" || die "no $FE_WT"
  VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 VITE_CARD_ART_BASE_URL="$CARD_ART" npm run build \
    || die "npm run build failed in $FE_WT"
  echo "built $FE_WT/dist at $(git -C "$FE_WT" rev-parse HEAD) for http://localhost:8080, card art from $CARD_ART"
}

cmd_spa_preview() {
  cd "$FE_WT" || die "no $FE_WT"
  VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 VITE_CARD_ART_BASE_URL="$CARD_ART" exec npx vite preview --port 4173 --strictPort
}

cmd_logs() {
  local label=${1:-} dir=${2:-$LOGS} file
  case "$label" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) die "usage: rig.sh logs <label> [dir]" ;; esac
  [ -d "$dir" ] || die "no directory $dir"
  file=$dir/backend-$label.log
  docker logs pd-backend > "$file" 2>&1 || die "no pd-backend container"
  echo "saved $file: $(/usr/bin/grep -c ' ERROR ' "$file") ERROR lines, $(/usr/bin/grep -c 'Started BelatroApplication' "$file") start(s)"
}

cmd_down() {
  docker rm -f pd-backend pd-mongo pd-redis pd-mailpit >/dev/null 2>&1
  docker network rm "$NET" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if [ -e "$RELEASE_WT" ]; then
    git -C "$BE_REPO" worktree remove --force "$RELEASE_WT" || echo "rig: could not remove $RELEASE_WT" >&2
  fi
  echo "rig down: containers, network and $RELEASE_WT removed; the image $IMAGE is kept"
}

case "${1:-}" in
  up) cmd_up ;;
  build-image) cmd_build_image "${2:-}" ;;
  image-checks) cmd_image_checks ;;
  dummy-env-check) cmd_dummy_env_check ;;
  backend-start) cmd_backend_start "${2:-}" ;;
  backend-stop) docker stop pd-backend >/dev/null && echo "pd-backend stopped" ;;
  backend-restart-after) cmd_backend_restart_after "${2:-}" ;;
  r4-checks) cmd_r4_checks ;;
  sigterm-check) cmd_sigterm_check ;;
  idle-check) cmd_idle_check ;;
  spa-build) cmd_spa_build ;;
  spa-check) cmd_spa_check ;;
  spa-preview) cmd_spa_preview ;;
  logs) cmd_logs "${2:-}" "${3:-}" ;;
  status) docker ps -a --filter name=pd- --format '{{.Names}}  {{.Status}}  {{.Ports}}' ;;
  down) cmd_down ;;
  *) echo "usage: rig.sh up | build-image <sha> | image-checks | dummy-env-check | backend-start [jwt-minutes] | backend-stop | backend-restart-after <seconds> | r4-checks | sigterm-check | idle-check | spa-build | spa-check | spa-preview | logs <label> [dir] | status | down" >&2
     exit 2 ;;
esac
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the SPA worktree's e2e/gameplay.mjs against the rig: the production SPA bundle on
# http://localhost:4173 (vite preview), the release image as pd-backend on :8080 and Mailpit on
# :8025. The pre-deploy gate (its plan Phase 8) ran it for pd-frontend; the UI redesign's gate (its
# plan Phase 11) runs it for ui-frontend against the combined release and keeps every log in that
# run's folder (OUT). Every run starts a fresh pd-backend first: its rate limits live in memory
# (signup is 20 per hour per IP), and a run must not inherit the previous run's sockets or timers.
#   run-harness.sh badinvite | full | xhr | renewal | restart | mobile | record
# The first six are the release gate. record is not: it plays one plain game with the view recorder
# on (E2E_RECORD_VIEWS=1), which saves seat 1's game frames in the SPA worktree as
# src/test/fixtures/views/recorded-<run>.json. Every gate run has the recorder off.
set -u
LOGS=/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/logs/pre-deploy
OUT=/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/Belatro/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-09-ui-redesign/release-gate
HARNESS=/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/ui-frontend/e2e/gameplay.mjs
RIG=$LOGS/rig.sh
mode=${1:-}
jwt_minutes=
export PLAYWRIGHT_CORE_DIR=$LOGS/pw/node_modules/playwright-core
# the SPA origin must be localhost:4173 (the backend's CORS origin); node-side calls use 127.0.0.1
export SPA_URL=http://localhost:4173 API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 MAILPIT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8025
export E2E_INVITE_CODE=rig-invite
unset E2E_CONFIRM_EMAIL E2E_SOCKJS_TRANSPORT E2E_RESTART_CMD E2E_EXPECT_RENEWAL E2E_REMATCH E2E_VIEWPORT E2E_LANDSCAPE_CHECK E2E_RECORD_VIEWS HEADLESS
case "$mode" in
  badinvite) export E2E_INVITE_CODE=not-the-rig-code ;;
  full)      export E2E_CONFIRM_EMAIL=1 E2E_REMATCH=1 ;;
  xhr)       export E2E_SOCKJS_TRANSPORT=xhr-streaming ;;
  renewal)   export E2E_EXPECT_RENEWAL=1; jwt_minutes=3 ;;
  restart)   export E2E_RESTART_CMD="bash $RIG backend-restart-after 60" ;;
  mobile)    export E2E_VIEWPORT=375x812 E2E_LANDSCAPE_CHECK=1 ;;
  record)    export E2E_RECORD_VIEWS=1 ;;
  *) echo "usage: run-harness.sh badinvite | full | xhr | renewal | restart | mobile | record" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
mkdir -p "$OUT" || exit 1
export E2E_ARTIFACTS=$OUT/harness-$mode
if [ "$(curl --noproxy '*' -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 http://localhost:4173/)" != 200 ]; then
  echo "run-harness: the SPA preview does not answer on http://localhost:4173 (rig.sh spa-build, then vite preview on 4173)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
bash "$RIG" backend-start $jwt_minutes || exit 1
out=$OUT/harness-$mode.json
err=$OUT/harness-$mode.stderr.txt
node "$HARNESS" > "$out" 2> "$err"
code=$?
bash "$RIG" logs "harness-$mode" "$OUT"
if [ "$mode" = badinvite ]; then
  # negative control: the run must fail, and for exactly this reason
  if [ "$code" = 1 ] && /usr/bin/grep -q 'FAILED: signup refused: Invalid invite code' "$err"; then
    echo "harness badinvite: the negative control held (signup refused: Invalid invite code)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "harness badinvite: the negative control FAILED (exit $code; see $err)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "harness $mode: exit $code (summary $out, log $err)"
exit "$code"
```

```js
// Three computer players for a game with the owner on the local rig (not part of any check), on the
// redesigned SPA (UI-redesign spec §7.4's names). Bot 1 creates the casual lobby ("Create lobby",
// then the sheet's "Create") and is seated in Team A; bots 2 and 3 join it from Lobbies and take the
// first "Sit here, team B"; the human joins from Lobbies too and taps "Sit here, team A" (bot 1's
// partner). Bot 1 starts the match once all four are seated. Bots bid with a simple trump rule,
// play a random legal card about a second after their turn starts, declare bela when asked, and
// vote "Play again" after a game. Runs until stopped.
// Usage: node bots.mjs <bot 1> <bot 2> <bot 3> [lobby name]
// (three existing rig accounts with the harness's password, e.g. players 2-4 of the last gate run)
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const { chromium } = require('/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/logs/pre-deploy/pw/node_modules/playwright-core');

const SPA = 'http://localhost:4173';
const BOTS = process.argv.slice(2, 5);
const LOBBY = process.argv[5] ?? "Claude's table";
const PASSWORD = 'e2e-password-123';
const PACE_MS = 1200;
const PHASE = { Bidding: 'BIDDING', Playing: 'PLAYING', 'Hand finished': 'HAND_COMPLETE', 'Game over': 'COMPLETED', Cancelled: 'CANCELLED' };
const SUIT = { HERC: 'Herc', KARA: 'Karo', PIK: 'Pik', TREF: 'Tref' };
const TRUMP_VALUE = { DECKO: 20, DEVETKA: 14, AS: 11, DESETKA: 10, KRALJ: 4, BABA: 3, OSMICA: 0, SEDMICA: 0 };

if (BOTS.length !== 3) {
    console.error('usage: node bots.mjs <bot 1> <bot 2> <bot 3> [lobby name]');
    process.exit(2);
}

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
const log = (who, what) => console.log(`${new Date().toISOString().slice(11, 19)} ${who}: ${what}`);
const escapeRegExp = (text) => text.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

async function waitUntil(check, timeoutMs, what) {
    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
    for (;;) {
        if (await check()) return;
        if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms: ${what}`);
        await sleep(250);
    }
}

const phaseOf = async (page) => {
    const value = await page.getByTestId('game-phase')
        .evaluate((el) => el.getAttribute('data-phase') ?? el.textContent, undefined, { timeout: 1000 })
        .catch(() => null);
    return value === null ? null : (PHASE[value.trim()] ?? value.trim());
};
const myTurn = (page) => page.getByTestId('your-turn').isVisible().catch(() => false);
// the hand cards and whether each may be played (the button's native disabled)
const handCards = async (page) => (await page.getByTestId('hand-card').evaluateAll((els) =>
    els.map((el) => ({ card: el.getAttribute('data-card'), enabled: !el.disabled })))).filter((c) => c.card);
// The point (10, 30) of a card's own face, in the strip the fan leaves exposed, as a click position
// measured from its bounding box: a fanned card is turned, so the point turns with it (as the harness).
const cardPoint = (card) => card.evaluate((el) => {
    const box = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    const transform = getComputedStyle(el).transform;
    const m = new DOMMatrixReadOnly(transform === 'none' ? undefined : transform);
    const scale = Math.hypot(m.a, m.b) || 1;
    const dx = (10 - el.offsetWidth / 2) * scale;
    const dy = (30 - el.offsetHeight / 2) * scale;
    return { x: box.width / 2 + (dx * m.a - dy * m.b) / scale, y: box.height / 2 + (dx * m.b + dy * m.a) / scale };
});

async function logIn(page, username) {
    await page.goto(`${SPA}/login`);
    await page.getByLabel('Username', { exact: true }).fill(username);
    await page.getByLabel('Password', { exact: true }).fill(PASSWORD);
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign In', exact: true }).click();
    await page.waitForURL('**/dashboard', { timeout: 15000 });
}

async function formLobby(host, guests) {
    await host.goto(`${SPA}/lobbies`);
    await host.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create lobby', exact: true }).click();
    const sheet = host.getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Create lobby', exact: true });
    await sheet.getByLabel('Lobby name', { exact: true }).fill(LOBBY);
    await sheet.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create', exact: true }).click();
    await host.waitForURL('**/lobby/**', { timeout: 15000 });
    const lobbyUrl = host.url();
    for (const [i, guest] of guests.entries()) {
        const bot = BOTS[i + 1];
        await guest.goto(`${SPA}/lobbies`);
        await guest.getByRole('button', { name: new RegExp(`^${escapeRegExp(LOBBY)}, host `) }).first().click({ timeout: 15000 });
        await guest.getByRole('dialog', { name: LOBBY, exact: true }).getByRole('button', { name: 'Join lobby', exact: true }).click();
        await guest.waitForURL('**/lobby/**', { timeout: 15000 });
        await guest.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sit here, team B', exact: true }).first().click({ timeout: 15000 });
        const mine = guest.getByRole('button', { name: `${bot} (you), team B`, exact: true });
        const busy = guest.getByTestId('lobby-table').locator('[aria-busy="true"]');
        await waitUntil(async () => (await mine.count()) === 1 && (await busy.count()) === 0, 15000, `${bot} sits in Team B`);
    }
    return lobbyUrl;
}

// Trump: the suit whose cards are worth most as trump (plus 5 per card); call it with a jack and one
// more honour or with four cards, otherwise pass. A dealer who must call names the best suit.
function chooseBid(cards, mustCall) {
    const score = {};
    for (const { card } of cards) {
        const [suit, rank] = card.split('-');
        score[suit] = (score[suit] ?? 0) + TRUMP_VALUE[rank] + 5;
    }
    const [best, value] = Object.entries(score).sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1])[0] ?? ['HERC', 0];
    const count = cards.filter(({ card }) => card.startsWith(`${best}-`)).length;
    const strong = value >= 50 || count >= 4;
    return mustCall || strong ? `Call ${SUIT[best]}` : 'Pass';
}

async function act(page, who) {
    const phase = await phaseOf(page);
    if (phase === 'COMPLETED') {
        const again = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Play again', exact: true });
        if (await again.isVisible().catch(() => false) && await again.isEnabled().catch(() => false)) {
            await again.click();
            log(who, 'wants a rematch (Play again)');
        }
        return;
    }
    if (phase === 'CANCELLED') return;
    if ((phase !== 'BIDDING' && phase !== 'PLAYING') || !(await myTurn(page))) return;
    await sleep(PACE_MS);
    if (!(await myTurn(page))) return;
    const cards = await handCards(page);
    if (phase === 'BIDDING') {
        const mustCall = await page.getByTestId('dealer-must-call').isVisible().catch(() => false);
        const choice = chooseBid(cards, mustCall);
        const button = page.getByRole('button', { name: choice, exact: true });
        if (!(await button.isVisible().catch(() => false))) return;
        await button.click();
        log(who, choice);
        await waitUntil(async () => !(await myTurn(page)) || (await phaseOf(page)) !== 'BIDDING', 5000, `${who}'s bid`).catch(() => {});
        return;
    }
    const playable = cards.filter((c) => c.enabled);
    if (!playable.length) return;
    const { card } = playable[Math.floor(Math.random() * playable.length)];
    const target = page.locator(`[data-testid="hand-card"][data-card="${card}"]`);
    await target.click({ position: await cardPoint(target) });
    const bela = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Play + Bela', exact: true });
    await waitUntil(async () => {
        if (await bela.isVisible().catch(() => false)) {
            await bela.click();
            log(who, 'declares bela');
        }
        return (await page.locator(`[data-testid="hand-card"][data-card="${card}"]`).count()) === 0;
    }, 5000, `${who}'s ${card} left the hand`).catch(() => {});
    log(who, `plays ${card}`);
}

async function main() {
    const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
    const pages = [];
    for (const bot of BOTS) {
        const page = await (await browser.newContext()).newPage();
        await logIn(page, bot);
        log(bot, 'signed in');
        pages.push(page);
    }
    const [host, ...guests] = pages;
    const lobbyUrl = await formLobby(host, guests);
    log('table', `lobby "${LOBBY}" ready at ${lobbyUrl}: open it from Lobbies, press Join lobby and tap "Sit here, team A"`);
    const start = host.getByRole('button', { name: /Start match/i });
    await waitUntil(async () => start.isEnabled().catch(() => false), 30 * 60000, 'the fourth player takes a seat');
    await sleep(1500);
    await start.click();
    log('table', 'match started');
    await Promise.all(pages.map((page) => page.waitForURL('**/game/**', { timeout: 30000 })));
    for (;;) {
        for (const [i, page] of pages.entries()) {
            try {
                await act(page, BOTS[i]);
            } catch (error) {
                log(BOTS[i], `skipped a beat: ${error.message.split('\n')[0]}`);
            }
        }
        await sleep(300);
    }
}

main().catch((error) => {
    console.error(`bots stopped: ${error.message}`);
    process.exit(1);
});
```

**How to judge a run:**
- `run-harness.sh` prints `harness <mode>: exit 0 (summary …, log …)` and, just before it, `saved …/release-gate/backend-harness-<mode>.log: <n> ERROR lines, <m> start(s)`.
- Read `RUN/release-gate/harness-<mode>.json` with the Read tool and compare it with the list for that mode. Never judge from console prose.
- Read every `ERROR` line of the backend log. One that comes from the run's own game or requests is a defect, even when the harness passed; the background re-arm of games left from earlier runs is not.
- On a non-zero exit, `harness-<mode>.stderr.txt` starts with `FAILED: <reason>`, and the screenshots show each seat. Then apply "When a run fails".
- In every positive mode:
  - `final.result` reads `Team <winner> wins <teamA>–<teamB>` (en dash); `final.matchDetails` equals `{teamA, teamB}`; the winner's score is ≥ 1001 and higher than the other's;
  - `final.storedHands.hands` = `trumpCalls` + 1, and every number in `final.storedHands.tricks` is 8 (the harness has already failed the run if a trick had no winner or a hand no summary: spec §6.3 on real matches);
  - `"recorded": null` (the recorder is off in every gate run).

`/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/Belatro/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-09-ui-redesign/release-gate/pr-body-backend.md`:

```markdown
The Stiglja UI redesign: backend. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-ui-redesign-design.md in Meawen/Belatro_FrontEnd_LukasSoloRewrite (§6).

Deploy order: this backend first, then the SPA (Meawen/Belatro_FrontEnd_LukasSoloRewrite, its own PR). The SPA works without the new fields, so this backend can go out on its own.

## Changes
- PublicGameView gains stateVersion, lastTrick, tricksWonA, tricksWonB, dealerId and serverNow (spec §6.1). stateVersion is a per-game Redis counter, belot:gamever:{gameId}, advanced by every BelotGameService.save with one Lua script (seeded with the epoch ms when missing, so it never goes backwards) and kept with the game key's TTL, which GameActivityAspect refreshes for both. A counter failure is logged and never stops the save.
- Every game broadcast reads the version, the game and the version again (three tries; skipped when they never agree, a later broadcast follows every save). The controller no longer broadcasts the game object it captured before the lock was released (play, bid, challenge, cancel); one broadcast's public and private frames carry one version.
- GET /user/findAll?sort=elo lists players with games first, by Elo, then games played, then username, and accounts with no games after them by username; any other value answers 400 {"error":"Unknown sort: <value>"} (spec §6.2).
- Structured moves: each hand's 8th trick gets its END_TRICK (winner, points, last-trick bonus), and no empty hand follows the last one. Stored moves are unchanged, so old matches are corrected when they are read (spec §6.3).

## Wire changes (additive; consumer: Belatro_FrontEnd_LukasSoloRewrite)
- PublicGameView, and PrivateGameView.publicPart: new trailing fields stateVersion (long), lastTrick ({leadPlayerId, plays, order, winnerId} or null), tricksWonA and tricksWonB (int), dealerId (String) and serverNow (epoch ms).
- GET /user/findAll: a new optional query parameter sort (elo).
- Behaviour fixes with the same wire shape: the after-action broadcasts carry a fresh read; /matches/{id}/structured-moves files the 8th trick under its own hand and emits no phantom hand.

No STOMP destination, existing route or existing field changes. The dormant sibling frontends ignore the new fields.

## One-way data changes
None. The new Redis keys belot:gamever:* expire with their game; an older image ignores them.

## Verification
- ./gradlew build --rerun-tasks on JDK 21: <UI_BE_TEST_COUNT> tests, 0 failures (735 at the pre-deploy head, plus the tests of every change above).
- The release gate on a local rig (Mongo 8 replica set, Redis 7, Mailpit) with this backend's image and the redesigned SPA's production bundle on a second origin: a refused invite code; whole four-seat games over WebSocket with confirmed mail, Match details and a rematch; over xhr-streaming; with 3-minute tokens renewed; across a 60-second backend restart; at 375x812 with one seat turned to 812x375. In every played-out game the structured moves held each hand's 8 tricks with their winners.
- Still to come before merging: the owner's play-test, a whole game with three bots on that rig.
- Not verifiable before production: the counter's Lua and TTL on Redis Cloud, more than one backend instance, and the clocks of real devices.
```

```markdown
The Stiglja UI redesign: SPA. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-ui-redesign-design.md; plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-ui-redesign.md.

Deploy order: the backend (Meawen/stiglja, its own PR) first, then this SPA on Cloudflare Pages with the new build variable VITE_CARD_ART_BASE_URL set (the pre-deploy runbook's Phase 9, amended for the card-art domain).

## Changes
- A design system: colour tokens, the system font with the Jersey 10 pixel face for titles and scores, pixel icons, the ui components, motion 13.4.4 for springs and shared-layout card flights (gsap, @gsap/react and @types/gsap removed).
- The shell: a phone tab bar and a desktop sidebar, the return path after sign-in and sign-up, the banners, the footer, a pixel favicon.
- The board: driven only by the server's views (frames accepted by stateVersion; snapshots snap), cards that fly from where they are, the trick's winner crowned and swept to its team's pile, a season per trump, Bela Blok, the won-trick peek, hand results and the end sheet, a compact landscape layout; /dev/board in dev builds only.
- Lobbies with a quick-look and a table to sit at; sign-in and sign-up on one panel; Home, Ranked and Match found; Match History and Match details on their own page (/matches/:id); Profile, Settings, Friends, the Leaderboard by Elo, Admin, Rules, Privacy and Terms.
- Removed: /play/mock, /play/realistic, src/MockComponents, gsap, and the dead code that went with the old screens.
- CI: VITE_CARD_ART_BASE_URL in the build, a guard that /dev/board never reaches dist/, and a bundle-size check.
- e2e/gameplay.mjs follows the new screens and gains a landscape turn and an opt-in view recorder; one recorded view sequence is under src/test/fixtures/views/.

## Backend contract consumed (Meawen/stiglja, deployed first)
The optional PublicGameView fields stateVersion, lastTrick, tricksWonA, tricksWonB, dealerId and serverNow (the SPA works without them), GET /user/findAll?sort=elo, and the corrected structured moves. No STOMP destination or backend route changes.

## New build setting
VITE_CARD_ART_BASE_URL, required by a production build like VITE_API_BASE_URL: the card art's origin, for example https://cards.stiglja.com/v1.

## Verification
- npm ci, npx tsc -b, npx vitest run (<UI_FE_TEST_FILES> files, <UI_FE_TEST_COUNT> tests passed; every behaviour the pre-deploy SPA's 395 tests pinned keeps a test) and npm run build with both variables.
- Playwright checks on macOS Chromium (local, not in CI): every route at 1440x900 and 375x812 and the board at 812x375 against the baselines, no sideways scroll at 375, hit-testing with every sheet closed, reduced motion, more contrast and forced colours, focus rings, and frame times under a 4x CPU throttle.
- The release gate on a local rig against the backend above, with this production bundle on a second origin: a refused invite code; whole four-seat games over WebSocket with confirmed mail, Match details and a rematch; over xhr-streaming; with 3-minute tokens renewed; across a 60-second backend restart; at 375x812 with one seat turned to 812x375.
- Still to come before merging: the owner's play-test, a whole game with three bots on that rig.
- Not verifiable before production: the card-art custom domain until its DNS step, iOS Safari's backdrop-filter, the frame rate on a real mid-range Android phone, and real screen readers.
```

## Phase B1: Game view fields on `PublicGameView` (backend lane)

**Goal.** The board reads the facts it used to guess from a run of views straight from every public view: who deals,
the server's clock, the tricks each team has won this hand, the last completed trick, and a per-game `stateVersion`
that lets the SPA drop stale and duplicate frames. On the wire this is additive: new trailing components on the
existing `PublicGameView` record, sent on the existing destinations; B1.5 is also a behaviour fix with the same wire
shape (the controller stops broadcasting a stale game). The SPA (Phase 3) tolerates the fields' absence, so this lane
deploys first and on its own (two-step rule, backend `CLAUDE.md`).

**Covers:** spec §6.1 (fields, producer rules 1–5, backend tests 1–7), §6.4; D-8; R-7 (TTL of the new key);
`RUN/explore/game-data.md` §2.1 (fan-out triggers GSC/TS/CTL/GS/REF) and §8 #2 (views regress: the controller
broadcast the game it captured before the lock was released). US-26, US-27, US-31, US-32, US-37 (data side).

**Repo and base.** Backend worktree `/Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/ui-backend`, branch `ui-redesign`
from `pre-deploy` @ `dc3fcf3` (created by Task 0.2). Every command runs from that worktree's root. Gradle runs
**outside the sandbox** (`dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`), one command per call with nothing else in it; Docker
Desktop must run (`*IT` start their own Redis and Mongo through Testcontainers; never the rig containers). Tests are
judged from `python3 /Users/lmiholic/IdeaProjects/stiglja-lanes/logs/pre-deploy/junit-summary.py . <Class>…`, which
reads `build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml`. A red step that fails at compile time is judged from Gradle's own
`error:` lines instead (the XML of an earlier run would still be there). Baseline: **735 tests, 0 failures**.

**Do-not-touch (respected by every task; checked in Task B.R):** `configs/SecurityConfig.java`,
`configs/WsConfig.java`, `configs/RedisConfig.java`, `pojo/gamelogic/BelotGame.java`, `SchedulerConfig.taskScheduler`,
the `@Query` on `repos/MatchRepo`, `equals`/`hashCode` in `models/`. No `BelotGame` field is added: the version
counter lives beside the game key in Redis, as `AbsenceCounters` and `GameOutcomeStore` do.

**Produces (wire, consumer `Belatro_FrontEnd_LukasSoloRewrite`; Phase 3 types them as optional):**

| JSON field on `PublicGameView` (and on `PrivateGameView.publicPart`) | Java type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `dealerId` | `String` | `g.getDealer().getId()`; null only for a game that was never started |
| `serverNow` | `long` | `System.currentTimeMillis()` when the view was built |
| `tricksWonA`, `tricksWonB` | `int` | completed tricks of the current hand won by Team A / Team B (0/0 from the deal until the first trick completes) |
| `lastTrick` | `LastTrickView` or `null` | `{leadPlayerId: String, plays: {playerId: {boja, rank}}, order: [playerId ×4], winnerId: String}`: the hand's last completed trick; `order` = the seats in turn order starting at `leadPlayerId`; null from the deal until the first trick of the hand completes; present through HAND_COMPLETE (and in COMPLETED/CANCELLED) |
| `stateVersion` | `long` | the value of the Redis counter `belot:gamever:{gameId}`, advanced by every `BelotGameService.save` after the game key is written; seeded with the epoch ms when missing, so it never goes backwards (owner decision O-1); 0 when no save has happened |

Java interfaces other code may use (exact):
- `record backend.belatro.dtos.LastTrickView(String leadPlayerId, Map<String, Card> plays, List<String> order, String winnerId)`
- `@Component backend.belatro.components.GameVersions(StringRedisTemplate)`: `long increment(String gameId, Duration ttl)` (one Lua script: seed a missing key with the epoch ms, `INCR`, `PEXPIRE`), `void expire(String gameId, Duration ttl)`, `long current(String gameId)`; `GameActivityAspect` refreshes the version key's TTL with the game key's
- `BelotGameService`: constructor `(RedisTemplate<String, BelotGame>, ApplicationEventPublisher, IMatchService, TaskScheduler, GameOutcomeStore, TurnDeadlines, GameVersions)`; `long stateVersion(String gameId)`; `PublicGameView toPublicView(BelotGame g, long version)`; `PrivateGameView toPrivateView(BelotGame g, Player p, long version)` (the one-argument forms stay and read the counter themselves).
- `GameSocketController`: every view it sends is built from `readFresh(gameId)`: the version, then the game, then the version again, retried while they differ (three tries); when they never agree the broadcast is skipped (a later one follows every save).

**Test ladder (Gradle, whole suite):** 735 → B1.1 738 → B1.2 742 → B1.3 749 → B1.4 756 → B1.5 762 → B2.1 767 → B3.1 770 → B.R 770.

### Task B1.1: The public view names the dealer and the time it was built (spec §6.1 `dealerId`, `serverNow`, tests 3 and 7; D-8; US-31)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameServiceViewFieldsTest.java`
- Modify: `src/main/java/backend/belatro/dtos/PublicGameView.java`, `src/main/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameService.java`
- Delete: —

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `BelotGameService.toPublicView(BelotGame)` (today `BelotGameService.java:364-443`), `BelotGame.getDealer()`
  (`@Getter`, `BelotGame.java:71-72`), test helper `DealtGames` (`src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/DealtGames.java`:
  seat 0 bids first, seat 3 is the dealer).
- Produces: `PublicGameView.dealerId()` (`String`) and `PublicGameView.serverNow()` (`long`), the record's two new
  last components. Wire: `"dealerId"`, `"serverNow"`.

**Old tests carried:** none (new fields; every existing `toPublicView` test runs unchanged).

**Why these tests.** The dealer is checked against the seating, not against `getDealer()` (that would be the code
under test): at a deal the dealer is the last seat of `seatingOrder` (`BelotGame.selectDealer`, `selectNextDealer`),
it does not move while the hand is played (even though `seatingOrder` rotates after every trick), and the next deal
hands it to the seat after it, which was the first bidder.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```java file=src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameServiceViewFieldsTest.java
package backend.belatro.services;

import backend.belatro.components.TurnDeadlines;
import backend.belatro.dtos.PublicGameView;
import backend.belatro.pojo.gamelogic.BelotGame;
import backend.belatro.pojo.gamelogic.Player;
import backend.belatro.pojo.gamelogic.enums.Boja;
import backend.belatro.pojo.gamelogic.enums.GameState;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisher;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.RedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.scheduling.TaskScheduler;

import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.within;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.mock;

/**
 * UI redesign spec §6.1: the facts the board reads straight from the public view instead of guessing
 * them from a run of views. Plain unit test: toPublicView reads only the BelotGame it is given, so the
 * collaborators are inert mocks (as in BelotGameServiceDeclarationsTest).
 */
class BelotGameServiceViewFieldsTest {

    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
    private final BelotGameService svc = new BelotGameService(
            (RedisTemplate<String, BelotGame>) mock(RedisTemplate.class),
            mock(ApplicationEventPublisher.class),
            mock(IMatchService.class),
            mock(TaskScheduler.class),
            mock(GameOutcomeStore.class),
            new TurnDeadlines());

    // ---------- dealerId (§6.1 test 3) ----------

    @Test
    void atTheDealTheDealerIsTheSeatThatBidsLast() {
        PublicGameView view = svc.toPublicView(DealtGames.dealt(DealtGames.QUARTE_BEATS_TIERCE));

        assertThat(view.dealerId()).as("dealerId at the deal: the last seat of seatingOrder")
                .isEqualTo(view.seatingOrder().get(3).getId());
    }

    @Test
    void theDealerKeepsTheDealThroughTheHandAndTheNextDealMovesItOneSeatOn() {
        BelotGame g = DealtGames.callTrump(DealtGames.dealt(DealtGames.QUARTE_BEATS_TIERCE), Boja.HERC);
        List<String> seats = g.getTurnOrder().stream().map(Player::getId).toList();   // seat 3 deals

        DealtGames.playLegalCards(g, 4);   // a trick completes and seatingOrder rotates to its winner
        assertThat(svc.toPublicView(g).dealerId()).as("dealerId after the first trick").isEqualTo(seats.get(3));

        DealtGames.playOutTheHand(g);
        assertThat(svc.toPublicView(g).dealerId()).as("dealerId between hands").isEqualTo(seats.get(3));

        g.startNextHandAfterWindow();
        assertThat(g.getGameState()).as("precondition: the next hand is dealt").isEqualTo(GameState.BIDDING);
        PublicGameView next = svc.toPublicView(g);
        assertThat(next.dealerId()).as("dealerId of the next hand: the seat after the old dealer")
                .isEqualTo(seats.get(0))
                .isEqualTo(next.seatingOrder().get(3).getId());
    }

    // ---------- serverNow (§6.1 test 7) ----------

    @Test
    void serverNowIsWhenTheViewWasBuilt() {
        PublicGameView view = svc.toPublicView(DealtGames.dealt(DealtGames.QUARTE_BEATS_TIERCE));

        assertThat(view.serverNow()).as("serverNow vs the test clock (ms)")
                .isCloseTo(System.currentTimeMillis(), within(1_000L));
    }
}
```

**Old tests carried:** none.

**Why these tests.** `order` and `winnerId` are checked for a trick led by each of the four seats, with cards whose
winner is plain (the only trump takes it). A played hand then checks the field against the engine's own outcome (the
first trick's winner leads the second), that it outlives the next lead (the reason the field exists: today the
completed trick vanishes from the wire at the next lead, `game-data.md` §8 #9), that it equals the eighth trick
still shown between hands, its wire keys, and that the next deal clears it.

```java edit=src/main/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameService.java
    /**
     * UI redesign §6.1: the hand's last completed trick, its play order and its winner; null until the
     * hand's first trick completes (completedTricks is emptied at the deal).
     */
    private static LastTrickView lastTrickOf(BelotGame g) {
        if (g.getCompletedTricks().isEmpty()) {
            return null;
        }
        Trick last = g.getCompletedTricks().getLast();
        // Play follows the turn order from the leader. The turn order only ever rotates, so its
        // current cycle is also the cycle the trick was played in.
        List<String> seats = g.getTurnOrder().stream().map(Player::getId).toList();
        int lead = seats.indexOf(last.getLeadPlayerId());
        List<String> order = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < seats.size(); i++) {
            order.add(seats.get((lead + i) % seats.size()));
        }
        return new LastTrickView(last.getLeadPlayerId(), Map.copyOf(last.getPlays()), order, last.determineWinner());
    }
```

### Task B1.4: Every save moves the game's state version, kept beside the game key with the game key's TTL (spec §6.1 `stateVersion`, producer rules 1, 4, 5, tests 4 and 6; owner decision O-1 (review-2 I-2); D-8; R-7; US-37)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/main/java/backend/belatro/components/GameVersions.java`, `src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/StateVersionIT.java`
- Modify: `src/main/java/backend/belatro/dtos/PublicGameView.java`, `src/main/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameService.java`,
  `src/main/java/backend/belatro/components/GameActivityAspect.java`,
  `src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameServiceViewFieldsTest.java`,
  `src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameServiceDeclarationsTest.java`,
  `src/test/java/backend/belatro/components/GameActivityAspectTest.java`,
  `src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameServiceMongoFailureTest.java`
- Delete: —

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `StringRedisTemplate` (Spring Boot's auto-configured one, as `AbsenceCounters` and `GameOutcomeStore`
  use; never the `RedisTemplate<String, BelotGame>` of the do-not-touch `RedisConfig`), `BelotGameService.ttlFor`
  (R-7: 24 h while running, 10 min once COMPLETED or CANCELLED).
- Produces: `GameVersions` (`long increment(String gameId, Duration ttl)`: one Lua script, seed a missing key with the
  epoch ms, `INCR`, `PEXPIRE`; `void expire(String gameId, Duration ttl)`; `long current(String gameId)`; key
  `belot:gamever:{gameId}`, a Redis string counter); `BelotGameService` constructor
  ends `(…, TurnDeadlines deadlines, GameVersions versions)`; `BelotGameService.stateVersion(String gameId)`;
  `GameActivityAspect` constructor `(RedisTemplate<String, BelotGame>, GameVersions)` (Lombok); `PublicGameView.stateVersion()`
  (`long`), the record's last component. Wire: `"stateVersion"`.

**Old tests carried:** `BelotGameServiceDeclarationsTest`, `GameActivityAspectTest` and `BelotGameServiceMongoFailureTest`
build `BelotGameService` (and the aspect) by hand: each gets `mock(GameVersions.class)` as the new last constructor
argument, nothing else; their assertions are unchanged. `BelotGameServiceMongoFailureTest` also gains one test.

**Design (spec §6.1 producer rules 1, 4, 5).**
- `save` writes the game key, **then** advances `belot:gamever:{id}` with **one Lua script** (owner decision O-1,
  review-2 I-2): if the key is missing, `SET` it to the current epoch ms; then `INCR`; then `PEXPIRE` with
  `ttlFor(state)`; **then** publishes `GameStateChangedEvent` and calls `finaliseMatch` as before. The GSC broadcast
  therefore already sees the new version. One script means the key never lacks a TTL (R-7), and a counter that was
  lost (evicted, flushed, expired early) restarts above every value it had, so the SPA never sees a game's versions
  go backwards. The first save of a game gives a version of about 1.8·10¹², far inside JavaScript's 2⁵³.
- The version key gets the game key's TTL at the same points: every `save`, and `GameActivityAspect`'s stamp after
  each `@GameAction` (which re-writes the game key with `ttlFor(state)` and now refreshes the version key's TTL too).
  A finished game's 10-min TTL applies to both.
- Repeated versions come only from clock-only re-broadcasts (the TS broadcast after a GSC one). `openChallengeWindow`
  calls `save`, so the 8th card moves the version three times (hand end, window, card).
- The key never matches the restart scan `belot:game:*` (`GameTimerRearmer`) nor `EmptyMatchReaper`'s `game:*`.
- A Redis failure on the counter is logged and swallowed: `save` goes on to the listeners and `finaliseMatch`, as the
  listeners' own failures do (Phase 5 review I-3). The new unit test pins that (spec-slip note: the spec is silent).
- In this task `toPublicView` still reads the counter itself, after its caller read the game; Task B1.5 moves that
  read in front of the game in every broadcast.

```java file=src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/StateVersionIT.java
        playOneCard(id);
        long afterEighth = version(id);
        assertThat(games.get(id).getGameState()).as("precondition: the 8th card ended the hand")
                .isEqualTo(GameState.HAND_COMPLETE);
        ChallengeWindows.expireNow(games, id);
        long afterExpiry = version(id);

        assertThat(games.get(id).getGameState()).as("precondition: the next hand is dealt").isEqualTo(GameState.BIDDING);
        assertThat(dealt).as("stateVersion after the first save").isPositive();
        assertThat(afterBid).as("stateVersion after the trump call").isGreaterThan(dealt);
        assertThat(afterCard).as("stateVersion after a card").isGreaterThan(afterBid);
        assertThat(afterEighth).as("stateVersion after the 8th card: three saves").isEqualTo(beforeEighth + 3);
        assertThat(afterExpiry).as("stateVersion after the window's expiry").isGreaterThan(afterEighth);
    }

    /** §6.1 test 6, first half. */
    @Test
    void theVersionKeyLivesAsLongAsTheGameKeyWhileTheGameRunsAndTenMinutesAfterACancel() {
        String id = savedDeal(false);
        callTrump(id);
        playOneCard(id);

        assertThat(ttl("belot:gamever:" + id)).as("TTL of the version key while the game runs (s)")
                .isBetween(23 * HOUR, 24 * HOUR)
                .isCloseTo(gameTtl(id), within(2L));

        games.cancelMatch(id, games.get(id).getTurnOrder().get(0).getId());

        assertThat(ttl("belot:gamever:" + id)).as("TTL of the version key after a cancel (s)").isBetween(1L, 600L);
    }

    @Test
    void aCompletedGamesVersionKeyKeepsAtMostTenMinutes() {
        String id = savedDeal(true);
        callTrump(id);
        while (games.get(id).getGameState() == GameState.PLAYING) {
            playOneCard(id);
        }
        ChallengeWindows.expireNow(games, id);   // R-48: the deciding hand's window, then the end
        assertThat(games.get(id).getGameState()).as("precondition: the hand ended the match")
                .isEqualTo(GameState.COMPLETED);

        assertThat(ttl("belot:gamever:" + id)).as("TTL of the version key after the game completed (s)")
                .isBetween(1L, 600L);
    }

    /** O-1: every save leaves the version key with the game key's TTL (one script: INCR and PEXPIRE together). */
    @Test
    void everySaveLeavesTheVersionKeyWithATtl() {
        String id = savedDeal(false);
        assertThat(ttl("belot:gamever:" + id)).as("TTL of the version key after the first save (s)")
                .isBetween(23 * HOUR, 24 * HOUR);
        callTrump(id);
        assertThat(ttl("belot:gamever:" + id)).as("TTL of the version key after the bid (s)")
                .isBetween(23 * HOUR, 24 * HOUR);
        playOneCard(id);
        assertThat(ttl("belot:gamever:" + id)).as("TTL of the version key after a card (s)")
                .isBetween(23 * HOUR, 24 * HOUR);
    }

    /** O-1: a counter lost mid-game (evicted, flushed) restarts above every version it had. */
    @Test
    void aLostCounterRestartsAboveEveryVersionItHad() {
        String id = savedDeal(false);
        callTrump(id);
        playOneCard(id);
        long before = version(id);
        strings.delete("belot:gamever:" + id);

        playOneCard(id);

        assertThat(version(id)).as("stateVersion after the counter was lost and a card was played")
                .isGreaterThan(before);
    }

    /**
     * §6.1 test 6, second half: GameActivityAspect re-stamps the game key after every @GameAction, also
     * one that saves nothing (an out-of-turn card is refused without a save), and refreshes both TTLs.
     */
    @Test
    void theActivityStampRefreshesTheVersionKeysTtlWithTheGameKeys() {
        String id = savedDeal(false);
        callTrump(id);                                   // seat 0 leads: seat 1 is out of turn
        belotGameRedisTemplate.expire("belot:game:" + id, Duration.ofSeconds(60));
        strings.expire("belot:gamever:" + id, Duration.ofSeconds(60));
        Player seat1 = games.get(id).getTurnOrder().get(1);

        games.playCard(id, seat1.getId(), seat1.getHand().get(0), false);

        assertThat(gameTtl(id)).as("precondition: the stamp refreshed the game key's TTL (s)")
                .isBetween(23 * HOUR, 24 * HOUR);
        assertThat(ttl("belot:gamever:" + id)).as("TTL of the version key after the stamp (s)")
                .isBetween(23 * HOUR, 24 * HOUR);
    }

    // ---------- helpers ----------

    /**
     * A fixed deal saved through the service (still BIDDING). With {@code endsThisHand} Team A
     * already holds 1001 points, so the first hand ends the match.
     */
    private String savedDeal(boolean endsThisHand) {
        BelotGame g = DealtGames.dealt(DealtGames.QUARTE_BEATS_TIERCE);
        if (endsThisHand) {
            g.getTeamA().addPoints(1001);
        }
        games.save(g);
        return g.getGameId();
    }

    /** Seat 0 bids first and calls HERC; it then leads. */
    private void callTrump(String id) {
        String seat0 = games.get(id).getCurrentLead().getId();
        controller.bid(id, new BidMsg(false, Boja.HERC), as(seat0));
    }

    /** The player to act plays their first legal card. */
    private void playOneCard(String id) {
        BelotGame g = games.get(id);
        controller.play(id, new PlayCardMsg(g.getLegalMoves().get(0), false), as(g.getCurrentPlayer().getId()));
    }

    /** The state version a view of the game carries now. */
    private long version(String id) {
        return games.toPublicView(games.get(id)).stateVersion();
    }

    /** Seconds left on a key of strings; -1 = no TTL, -2 = no key. */
    private long ttl(String key) {
        return strings.getExpire(key, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
    }

    /** Seconds left on the game key. */
    private long gameTtl(String id) {
        return belotGameRedisTemplate.getExpire("belot:game:" + id, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
    }

    private static Principal as(String username) {
        return () -> username;
    }
}
```

```java file=src/main/java/backend/belatro/components/GameVersions.java
package backend.belatro.components;

import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.script.RedisScript;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * UI redesign spec §6.1: each game's state version, the Redis string counter belot:gamever:{gameId},
 * kept beside the game key as AbsenceCounters does (BelotGame gets no field). BelotGameService.save
 * advances it after every write of belot:game:{gameId}; it gets that key's TTL wherever the key gets
 * one (save, GameActivityAspect), so it expires with the game (R-7). It never goes backwards. Every view carries the version read
 * before the game, so a view never carries a version newer than its state; the SPA drops frames whose
 * version it has already passed.
 */
@Component
public class GameVersions {

    private static final String PREFIX = "belot:gamever:";

    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;

    public GameVersions(StringRedisTemplate redis) {
        this.redis = redis;
    }

    /**
     * Owner decision O-1 (review-2 I-2): one script, so the key never lacks a TTL (R-7). A missing counter
     * (a new game, or one lost to an eviction or a flush) starts at the current epoch ms, so it restarts
     * above every version it had; then INCR; then PEXPIRE with the game key's TTL.
     */
    private static final RedisScript<Long> ADVANCE = RedisScript.of(
            "if redis.call('EXISTS', KEYS[1]) == 0 then redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) end "
                    + "local v = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1]) "
                    + "redis.call('PEXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[2]) "
                    + "return v",
            Long.class);

    /** The game was just written: one version more, living as long as the game key ({@code ttl}). */
    public long increment(String gameId, Duration ttl) {
        Long v = redis.execute(ADVANCE, List.of(PREFIX + gameId),
                String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis()), String.valueOf(ttl.toMillis()));
        return v == null ? 0 : v;
    }

    /** The game key's TTL was refreshed without a new state: the version key gets the same TTL. */
    public void expire(String gameId, Duration ttl) {
        redis.expire(PREFIX + gameId, ttl);
    }

    /** The game's current version; 0 before its first save. */
    public long current(String gameId) {
        String v = redis.opsForValue().get(PREFIX + gameId);
        return v == null ? 0 : Long.parseLong(v);
    }
}
```

### Task B1.5: Every broadcast reads the version before the game; the controller stops sending the game it captured (spec §6.1 producer rules 2–4, tests 4 and 5; D-8; `game-data.md` §8 #2; US-26, US-27, US-37)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/test/java/backend/belatro/controllers/GameSocketControllerFreshReadTest.java`
- Modify: `src/main/java/backend/belatro/controllers/GameSocketController.java`, `src/main/java/backend/belatro/services/BelotGameService.java`,
  `src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/StateVersionIT.java`, `src/test/java/backend/belatro/controllers/GameSocketControllerTest.java`
- Delete: —

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `BelotGameService.stateVersion(String)` and `get(String)` (Task B1.4).
- Produces: `BelotGameService.toPublicView(BelotGame g, long version)` and `toPrivateView(BelotGame g, Player p, long version)`
  (the one-argument forms stay, read the counter themselves and are no longer used by any broadcast);
  `GameSocketController` builds **every** view it sends (GSC, TS, GS, the four controller-after-action sites, `/refresh`,
  both `@SubscribeMapping` snapshots) from `readFresh(gameId)`, and the public view and all private views of one
  broadcast carry the same version. `readFresh` returns null when the version moved during each of its three reads;
  the caller then sends nothing (rule 2: a later fan-out follows every save).

**Old tests carried:** `GameSocketControllerTest`: its `@BeforeEach` stubs move to the new signatures
(`toPublicView(any(), anyLong())`, `toPrivateView(any(), any(), anyLong())`) and stub `svc.get("g42")`, because
`play` and `bid` now re-read the game instead of using the one the service returned; its four tests and their
assertions are unchanged. `StateChangeListenersTest.theBroadcastLogsAFailureWhenAGameChangesState` runs unchanged
(the fresh read still calls `get`, which throws there).

**The bug (spec §6.1 rule 2; `game-data.md` §2.1, §8 #2).** `play`, `bid`, `challenge` and `cancel` broadcast the
`BelotGame` the service returned, after the game lock was released (`GameSocketController.java:93-96, 107-111,
116-120, 196-197`). Another move can land in between; with B1.4's code that broadcast
then carries the **newer** version with the **older** state, the SPA accepts it, and drops the real newer state as a
duplicate. The fix, for all readers:
- `readFresh(gameId)` (spec rule 2, "exact read"): read the version, then the game, then the version again; while
  they differ, read again, three tries in all; if they still differ, skip this broadcast. `save` writes the game
  before the version, so a view never carries a version newer than its state. (One case stays: a read that falls
  between a save's game write and its counter step sees the new state with the old version. The SPA takes that frame
  as a duplicate of the version it has, §5.3.1 item 2, and the save's own broadcast follows; see the spec-slip note in
  `phase-B.notes.md`.)
- The four controller sites call `fanOutGameState(id)`, the same fresh-read path GSC, TS and GS use.
- `/refresh` and both subscription snapshots use `readFresh` too.
- The version is read once per broadcast and passed into `toPublicView(g, version)` / `toPrivateView(g, p, version)`;
  before, `toPrivateView` rebuilt the public part per seat and could read a different version per frame.
- Rule 3 holds: every `save` is followed by a broadcast built after both writes (GSC, and the TS that `save` itself
  publishes on a return to BIDDING, come after them; every other TS fires after `save` returns). Rule 4: the TS re-arm broadcast after a GSC one repeats the version, with only `turnExpiresAt`
  changed (the SPA merges the clock fields).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing integration test**

The test builds its own `GameSocketController` around the real service, with a `SimpMessagingTemplate` that records

```java edit=src/test/java/backend/belatro/services/StateVersionIT.java
     * and its lock released, but before its broadcast. That broadcast carries the newer state with that

    @Test
    void theBroadcastAfterAnActionCarriesTheNewerStateWithItsExactVersion() {
        String id = savedDeal(false);
        callTrump(id);
        BelotGame before = games.get(id);
        String leader = before.getCurrentPlayer().getId();
        long[] savedWithOneCard = new long[1];
        List<Object> sent = new ArrayList<>();

        AbsenceCounters nextCardFirst = new AbsenceCounters(strings) {
            @Override
            public void reset(String gameId, String username) {
                savedWithOneCard[0] = games.stateVersion(gameId);
                BelotGame g = games.get(gameId);
                games.playCard(gameId, g.getCurrentPlayer().getId(), g.getLegalMoves().get(0), false);
                super.reset(gameId, username);
            }
        };
        GameSocketController recorded = new GameSocketController(games,
                new SimpMessagingTemplate((message, timeout) -> sent.add(message.getPayload())),
                matchService, nextCardFirst);

        recorded.play(id, new PlayCardMsg(before.getLegalMoves().get(0), false), as(leader));

        long savedWithTwoCards = games.stateVersion(id);
        assertThat(savedWithTwoCards).as("precondition: the second card moved the version").isGreaterThan(savedWithOneCard[0]);
        PublicGameView broadcast = sent.stream().filter(PublicGameView.class::isInstance)
                .map(PublicGameView.class::cast).findFirst().orElseThrow();
        assertThat(broadcast.currentTrick().getPlays())
                .as("cards on the table in the controller's broadcast (the older state shows 1)").hasSize(2);
        assertThat(broadcast.stateVersion()).as("the broadcast's version: the newer state's own")
                .isEqualTo(savedWithTwoCards);
        assertThat(sent.stream().filter(PrivateGameView.class::isInstance).map(PrivateGameView.class::cast).toList())
                .as("the broadcast's private frames, all at the public frame's version (§6.1 test 4)").hasSize(4)
                .allSatisfy(p -> assertThat(p.publicPart().stateVersion()).isEqualTo(broadcast.stateVersion()));
    }
```

```java edit=src/main/java/backend/belatro/controllers/GameSocketController.java
    /**
     * UI redesign §6.1 rule 2, the exact read every view this controller sends is built from: the state
     * version, then the game, then the version again, retried while they differ, three tries in all.
     * BelotGameService.save writes the game before the version, so a view never carries a version newer
     * than its state. Null when a save moved the version during every try: the caller then sends nothing,
     * and the broadcast that follows every save carries the state.
     */
    private VersionedGame readFresh(String gameId) {
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
            long version = svc.stateVersion(gameId);
            BelotGame game = svc.get(gameId);
            if (svc.stateVersion(gameId) == version) {
                return new VersionedGame(version, game);
            }
        }
        LOGGER.info("Skipped a broadcast of game {}: a save moved its version during every read", gameId);
        return null;
    }
```

## Phase B2: Leaderboard order on `GET /user/findAll` (backend lane)

**Goal.** The Leaderboard (spec §4.12, Phase 9) ranks players by Elo on the server, across pages, instead of
re-sorting one page on the client. One additive, optional query parameter; the route, its default order and its
response shape are unchanged, so today's SPA (which never sends `sort`) is unaffected.

**Covers:** spec §6.2, §4.12 (data side: "the request carries `sort=elo`"); owner decision O-3 (review-2 M-14); D-28; US-50.

**Produces (wire, consumer `Belatro_FrontEnd_LukasSoloRewrite`):** `GET /user/findAll?page&size&q&sort`:
- `sort` absent: by `username` ascending (today);
- `sort=elo` (owner decision O-3, review-2 M-14): players with `gamesPlayed > 0` first, by `eloRating` descending,
  then `gamesPlayed` descending, then `username` ascending; then the accounts with no game, by `username` ascending
  (their starting Elo must not outrank active players). `q` (case-insensitive literal substring of the username) and
  paging (`page`, `size` clamped as today) apply to that whole order; a page can span both parts;
- any other value, the empty one included: **400** with the backend's usual body `{"error":"Unknown sort: {value}"}`
  (`BadRequestException` → `GlobalExceptionHandler.handleBadRequest`).
- Java: `UserService.listSummaries(int page, int size, String q, String sort)` (was three parameters; its only caller
  is `UserController.getAllUsers`, which gains `@RequestParam(required = false) String sort`).

```java file=src/test/java/backend/belatro/controllers/UserListSortIT.java
import backend.belatro.context.AbstractSecurityIT;
import backend.belatro.context.TestTokens;
import backend.belatro.models.User;
import backend.belatro.repos.UserRepo;
import backend.belatro.security.JwtTokenProvider;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
```
